text:
maria: Heads up — deploy-bot flagged a P95 latency spike on model-serving-prod canary right after the rollout started. Change window is still open (09:00-11:00 PST). Metrics: https://metrics.redwood.internal/d/serving/canary-p95

deploy-bot: ALERT: canary failure threshold exceeded. metric=latency_p95 value=420ms threshold=300ms. canary_id=canary-2026-03-20-09:12. Recommend: reduce traffic to 0% and revert to pinned version v1.3.2. (automated suggestion) :rotating_light:

jordan: ok — can we confirm whether we should pin traffic back to v1.3.2 (traffic-split) or do a full rollback of pods? what's the minimal-impact path? @maria

maria: prefer pinning traffic first so we don't kill warm caches. follow runbook step 2.1 and 2.3 for partial-backout. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/backout-canary-v2 (see "traffic split" section)

lee: pinging ops-runbooks-bot to paste the exact commands for traffic split and rollback. need quick copy/paste for oncall.

ops-runbooks-bot: Runbook snippet (recommended sequence):

```
# reduce canary traffic to 0%
redwoodctl traffic split \ 
  --service=model-serving-prod \ 
  --from=canary-2026-03-20-09:12 \ 
  --to=stable \ 
  --percent=0

# if traffic split not supported, roll back to pinned image
redwoodctl deploy rollback --service=model-serving-prod --to-version=v1.3.2
```

Follow verification steps: wait 60s for stats, confirm p95 < 300ms, then fully scale down canary.

maria: I'm running the traffic-split now. executing command and will watch metrics. @jordan please stand by to promote if green.

maria: `> redwoodctl traffic split --service=model-serving-prod --from=canary-2026-03-20-09:12 --to=stable --percent=0`

deploy-bot: ACTION: Traffic split applied. new canary traffic=0%. Monitoring for 2 minutes.

lee: copying verification checklist here: check APM traces for spike, inspect request queue length, confirm no user-facing errors via /health endpoint, ensure canary pods drain gracefully.

jordan: seeing p95 drop to 180ms after ~90s. good sign. any errors in logs? @maria

maria: quick grep shows transient 5xx during peak, now quiet. not seeing commit-related exceptions.

release-coordinator: updating release notes: marking canary as "aborted, pinned to v1.3.2; investigating latency regression in v1.4.0" and notifying product. docs link: https://docs.redwood.com/releases/2026-03-20

maria: plan for next steps: open a rollback-incident ticket, collect logs and perf traces, kick off bisect of the changes in v1.4.0. For now we remain pinned to v1.3.2 in prod and will not reattempt until root cause is understood.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK STATUS: traffic pinned to stable version v1.3.2. canary instances scaled to 0%. Closing automated alert.

jordan: thanks — nice and surgical. I'll file the postmortem draft and assign followups. :thumbsup:

maria: thanks team. if anything regresses I'll re-open thread.
